PersonaQuery — grounded RAG over personal documents
**What it is:** A retrieval-augmented generation assistant that answers questions about Rudra strictly from his own documents — resume, research paper, patent, transcripts and project docs — with inline citations and prompt-injection guardrails. It powers the "Ask AI" assistant embedded in the portfolio site. **Repository layout:** FastAPI backend (`app/backend`), Next.js frontend (`app/frontend-next`), deployed backend on Render and frontend on Cloudflare Pages (https://rudrajoshi.dev). **Retrieval pipeline:** - Dense embeddings: `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` via FastEmbed (ONNX Runtime), 384-dimensional, cosine similarity; ColBERT v2 late-interaction reranking - Sparse keyword search: BM25 (Okapi, via `rank-bm25`) - Fusion: Reciprocal Rank Fusion, k=60 — chosen because it needs no score calibration between BM25 and cosine, which are not on comparable scales - Section-aware chunking with per-document-type profiles: resumes and transcripts chunk finely at 90–110 words with atomic bullet grouping, papers use 220-word windows - Vector store: NumPy matrix plus JSONL chunks. No external vector database. **Generation:** Qwen3.8-27B on the Groq free tier (OpenAI-compatible API) at temperature 0.2; internal query expansion

HealthEcho — symptom analysis chatbot
**What it is:** A web app where users describe symptoms in plain text and receive brief health advice generated by a hosted LLM. **Architecture:** Next.js 15 frontend (React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS) posting to an Express.js backend, which calls Together AI's `Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` and returns the advice, rendered with a typewriter animation. **Endpoints:** - `GET /api/health/check` — health check - `POST /api/analyze/symptoms` — accepts `{ symptoms }`, returns `{ status, advice }` **Deployment:** local development only at time of writing — no Docker, no CI/CD.

JobPilot / job-agent — multi-agent job application pipeline
**What it is:** A five-layer multi-agent system that automates the job application pipeline, from sourcing listings to tailoring documents and applying. **Architecture (from ARCHITECTURE.md):** - **Layer 1 — agents:** source, normalizer, match, resume, cover letter, QA, apply - **Layer 2 — guardrails engine** (`core/guardrails.py`): wraps every agent call. Input checks are schema validation, PII detection (passwords/tokens in prompts), token-budget warnings above 8000 tokens, and a rate limiter enforcing 5 seconds between API calls. Output checks are a hallucination detector for fabricated companies/dates/skills, output schema validation, a quality floor on minimum word count, and a cost tracker logging tokens and running spend. - **Layer 3 — skill hooks** (`core/skill_hooks.py`) - **Layer 4 — dynamic orchestration** (`agents/master_agent.py`): priority queue, routing, retry logic, skill integration - **Layer 5 — strategic agent** (`agents/strategic_agent.py`): weekly performance analysis and recommendations **Model routing:** writing agents (resume tailoring in LaTeX, cover letter generation via a critic-actor loop, strategic role targeting) run on Claude Opus; routing and utility agents

Deep Reinforcement Learning — algorithm benchmarking study
**What it is:** A comparative analysis of deep RL algorithms in continuous action spaces — DDPG, TD3, SAC and PPO — structured as a set of research questions. **Structure:** six research-question directories (RQ-1 through RQ6) covering basic algorithm performance, comparative analysis, advanced performance metrics and extended results, plus per-algorithm analysis directories: `DDPG_analysis`, `TD3_Analysis`, `SAC_Cont_Analysis`, `PPO_Cont_Analysis`. **Focus:** reward convergence, training stability, and sample efficiency across random seeds — the axes on which these algorithms actually differ in practice, as opposed to headline final scores. **Stack:** Python 3.7+, OpenAI Gym and MuJoCo environments. text:
Cognitive-Chair — brain-sensing wheelchair
**What it is:** An AI-based brain-sensing wheelchair for paraplegic and quadriplegic users, controlled through EEG and EOG signals (via a brain-computer interface) instead of the joystick a conventional electric wheelchair requires — aimed at users who cannot operate a joystick at all, not just at reducing joystick precision requirements. **How it works, at a high level:** electrodes pick up brainwave activity (the paper works with the standard Gamma/Beta/Alpha/Theta/Delta EEG bands), a processing pipeline extracts features and decodes intended movement from that signal, and the decoded command drives the wheelchair's motor controller. The system architecture follows the general BCI pattern — sense, decode, act — applied specifically to wheelchair navigation. **Recognition:** Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST-2022), organised by the Centre of Excellence – Artificial Intelligence. **Publication:** IEEE Xplore — https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10065338 **Co-authors:** Kshitij Joshi, Abhilasha Vyas, Smit Joshi and others, with Rudra Joshi as a co-author.
